title: Maximum period of the binary Lemire characteristic-delta convolution
statement: For every integer n >= 3, put ell=ceil(n/2)-1 and N=2^n-1. On Z/N, let delta_j be the GF(2)-valued indicator of residues whose canonical n-bit representative has Hamming weight j. Then the convolution product Gamma=product_(j=1)^ell (delta_0+delta_j) has least translation period N.

provenance.source: Axeyum gf2-lemire lane; Tuxanidy--Wang characteristic-delta reduction

notes: This is a deliberately stronger conjectural sufficient condition, not a promoted finite computation. ADR-0558 identifies the exact weaker criterion: applying product_(p|n)(1+tau_(2^(n/p)-1)) to Gamma is nonzero. Fourier inversion proves that this difference is nonzero exactly when an admissible exact-degree element exists. The older single-period criterion is equivalent only for prime-power n; at mixed-divisor degrees its exponent subgroup overcovers the union of proper subfields. Exact native convolution has maximum period for n=3 through 12, and an independent direct GF(2^n) characteristic-polynomial oracle agrees through n=8. Those bounded rows are controls, not evidence for the universal claim. Each individual factor has maximum period by the binary zero-coefficient case of Hansen--Mullen, but that property does not generally survive convolution of distinct factors: at n=8 the product through the middle weight j=4 has period 15 rather than 255. No proof operation is registered.
